conventions: Keep changes minimal and aligned with the existing repo helper seam instead of creating parallel orchestration surfaces.
Use the Linux-first workspace flow already documented in README.md as the supported HC-203 target.
Acceptance validation must follow the documented .env path instead of sourcing .env.example directly.
Server defaults remain workspace-local: logs/, storage/, and storage/server_identity.json unless env overrides are set.
Maintain command references consistently across README.md, client/AGENTS.md, server/AGENTS.md, and tester-facing guidance.
Treat README.md, client/AGENTS.md, server/AGENTS.md, and plans/08-tester-onboarding.md as the explicit HC-203 parity checklist set.

hard: Scope is standardizing the HayChat MVP start and stop workflow, not installing PostgreSQL globally.
Acceptance requires commands or helpers plus basic startup and shutdown guidance matching supported docs.
Do not assume control of the system PostgreSQL service lifecycle beyond HayChat-specific usage.
Keep the implementation minimal and consistent with the existing repo style.
Prefer helper scripts or task commands that work on Linux in this workspace.
soft: Prefer extending or tightening run-test-server.sh over adding a second orchestration entrypoint.
Reuse HC-201, HC-202, and HC-106 artifacts as prerequisites rather than recreating them.
Keep the current manual client launch stance if explicit `odin run client` guidance is sufficient to remove startup-order guesswork.
Treat explicit client-launch proof as part of acceptance even if the helper remains server-centric.
compatibility: README.md already documents bootstrap, start, bootstrap-start, start-background, wait-ready, stop, bootstrap-start-background, and hc118-gate commands.
run-test-server.sh already implements bootstrap, foreground start, background start, readiness waiting, and stop behavior.
client/AGENTS.md currently exposes `odin run client` as the direct client launch command, while server/AGENTS.md exposes `odin run server` as the direct server run command.
.env.example already defines the supported local server environment baseline for HC-202.
setup-dev-env.sh provisions PostgreSQL and default HayChat DB credentials during supported clean-machine bootstrap, but that script is not a runtime lifecycle manager.
security_requirements: Do not commit secrets or API keys.
Keep database credentials env-driven through .env.example and shell exports.
Do not stop or modify unrelated host databases while standardizing the HayChat workflow.
Preserve workspace-local runtime paths unless explicit env overrides are set.

patterns: run-test-server.sh is the owning seam for repo-supported MVP server bootstrap and lifecycle commands.
README.md is already the effective source of truth for the local MVP workflow, even where backlog issue text lags behind current implementation.
setup-dev-env.sh owns supported dependency bootstrap for Linux-first clean-machine setup, not day-to-day environment start or stop.
Client startup is currently documented as explicit odin run client commands rather than helper-managed orchestration.

gotchas.text: HC-203 backlog wording still implies broader orchestration than the current clarified scope allows, especially around PostgreSQL service control.
README.md and run-test-server.sh already advertise more helper functionality than plans/05-developer-experience.md currently summarizes.
Client launch remains manual in the documented flow, so acceptance may be satisfied by explicit guidance rather than new automation if sequencing is unambiguous.
Reviewer follow-up requires T4 validation to prove both the documented .env workflow and the documented server-then-client launch order, not just helper-managed server startup.
Reviewer follow-up also requires server/AGENTS.md to be inside the explicit parity set, and requires T1 and T3 outputs to name exact commands and exact aligned files instead of qualitative summaries.

prior_decisions.decision: Keep run-test-server.sh as the owning lifecycle seam for HC-203.
rationale: The script already implements the relevant start, readiness, and stop behavior.
Adding another orchestration surface would create drift without improving acceptance coverage.

prior_decisions.decision: Treat PostgreSQL availability as a prerequisite, not a lifecycle to be started and stopped by HC-203 helpers.
rationale: User clarifications explicitly narrow scope away from global PostgreSQL service control.
The host may be running unrelated databases, so aggressive lifecycle commands would be unsafe.

prior_decisions.decision: Reuse HC-201, HC-202, and HC-106 artifacts instead of recreating prerequisite setup paths.
rationale: setup-dev-env.sh, .env.example, and auth_bootstrap.sql already form the upstream contract for the local MVP workflow.
HC-203 acceptance is about standardizing run guidance and helper commands around that contract.

prior_decisions.decision: Treat the README .env path and documented client launch order as acceptance-critical validation inputs for HC-203.
rationale: Reviewer findings show that validating only the server helper leaves the startup workflow incomplete.
Doc-parity proof is incomplete when validation bypasses the documented .env path by sourcing .env.example directly.

prior_decisions.decision: Use README.md, client/AGENTS.md, server/AGENTS.md, and plans/08-tester-onboarding.md as the final HC-203 parity checklist set.
rationale: Reviewer follow-up explicitly adds server/AGENTS.md to the acceptance-facing validation scope.
These four docs are the visible workflow contract surfaces for helper commands, client launch stance, and shutdown guidance.
